messages:
nina: Quick proposal — add a fallback-priority matrix to the routing service + console so low-tier customers automatically route to cheaper model variants when cost thresholds hit. Also enforce a per-request token-cost cap that triggers fallback instead of hard 429. Thoughts?

kevin: +1 on matrix. We need to be careful about quality regressions though — should be per-route and per-region. i.e. some regions might prefer latency over cost.

sam: Sketch of the shape I'd propose for the routing API (very rough):
```
RouteConfig: {
  id: string,
  tier: ["free","starter","pro","enterprise"],
  region_policies: { region: { fallback_priority: ["model-a-q4","model-b-q8","model-a-fp16"], token_cost_cap: 0.002 } }
}
```
This keeps fallback policy close to route config so rollout service can target routes.

maya: How do we enforce token_cost_cap at runtime? two options: 1) estimate token cost pre-dispatch and choose variant, 2) stream and if we exceed, switch mid-stream (messy). I'd prefer pre-dispatch estimate with conservative upper bound.

jenni: From Console/UX side: we should show expected cost delta and latency delta for each fallback option inline (small sparkline + sample prompts). Also allow per-customer override toggle. Wireframe: slider for "cost cap" with suggested presets per tier.

kevin: Telemetry we need: fallback_count, fallback_rate_by_tier, avg_tokens_saved, cost_saved_usd, p95_latency_by_variant, quality_regression_alerts (comparing F1/ROUGE on eval-set). Add a tag for "policy_applied" in traces so we can split metrics easily.

sam: Internal API debate — embed fallback into RouteConfig vs separate FallbackPolicy resource. Pros of separate: reuse across routes and simpler diffs. Pros of embedded: faster lookup at runtime and easier canary per-route. Leaning embedded but we should make the schema shareable.

nina: For canary/rollout: default ordering when capacity constrained should be: pinned model (customer override) -> preferred variant -> cheaper variant -> cross-region fallback. We should let policy express priority order explicitly.

maya: Edge case: what if cheaper variant fails hallucination/regression checks during eval? We need automatic disable of that variant for all tiers until fixed, and a metric that counts "fallback quality incidents".

kevin: For cost accounting, runtime should emit estimated_token_cost_pre_dispatch and actual_token_cost_post_dispatch. That lets Optimize recommend quantization or batching changes.

jenni: UX ask: add a "what-if" sim mode in Console: pick a sample customer, apply cost-cap, run N prompts and show projected monthly $ impact + expected changes in latency/quality. Useful for sales.

ops-bot: RFC created: /docs/rfc-2026-fallback-priority-matrix.md (assigned to @sam, due 2026-03-05) :white_check_mark:

sam: Action items: 1) I will draft the RFC with both API shapes and perf tradeoffs, 2) kevin will mock telemetry events and required labels, 3) jenni will prototype console control and what-if UI, 4) maya will prototype runtime pre-dispatch estimator. We should sync next Tue.

nina: Nice — if everyone agrees I'll carve a small spike (2d) to validate pre-dispatch token-cost estimation accuracy on current traffic profiles. :thumbsup:
